transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, what brings me in is just this... this constant restless feeling I've been having. It’s like I’m wound way too tight and I just can’t fully settle down, even when I’m supposed to be doing something really calm. 

Like, if I'm sitting through a planning meeting at work—I'm a retail buyer, so we have these endless strategy meetings. Actually, just last Tuesday we were going over the spring inventory and the vendor was pushing these really uninspired floral prints. I mean, the fabric quality from them has just completely tanked since last year, and I keep telling my manager we need to source from somewhere else, but it's like talking to a wall. It’s incredibly frustrating when you know the customers are going to complain about the stitching falling apart after one wash. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, settling down. I can't even do it on my own time, like when I'm painting, or doing yoga. I only started yoga because my sister kept nagging me about it. She lives out in Sedona now and she’s gotten super into the whole wellness retreat lifestyle. I went to visit her for her birthday last year and the red rocks were gorgeous, but the heat is just unbelievable out there. I really don't know how anyone functions in that kind of sun. But yeah... I just always feel wound up and restless, even when I'm trying to just quietly do my yoga.
Do you find yourself having recurring thoughts that are hard to stop thinking about?

Recurring thoughts? Um, no, not really. I don't think I get stuck on one specific thing like that. If anything, my brain just kind of bounces from one thing to the next before I can even dwell on it. 

Like, I'll be thinking about what to make for dinner, and then I'll remember I need to pick up my dry cleaning, which reminds me of this beautiful silk blouse I completely ruined last month. It was my absolute favorite one, this gorgeous emerald green. Green is definitely my color. I was actually just telling my niece that she should wear more jewel tones, especially with her complexion. She’s a sophomore in college now, studying communications, which I honestly think is just so vague, you know? Like, what do you even do with a communications degree these days? I told her she really needs to look into supply chain management because that's where the actual job security is. The logistics issues we've had at work with overseas shipping have been a total nightmare for the last few years, and you really need people who know how to navigate customs... 

But, oh, sorry, what were we talking about? Thoughts getting stuck? Yeah, no, I don't really have that problem. They just keep moving.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Act on impulse? Um, well, I don't know if I'd say I do things without thinking *at all*. I mean, I don't think I do. Maybe sometimes? 

Actually, speaking of doing things without thinking, my husband just bought this massive espresso machine for the kitchen counter. Just completely out of the blue. He didn't even measure the space under the cabinets first, so now we have to pull it all the way out to the edge just to put the beans in. It’s a total eyesore, honestly. And he doesn't even drink espresso! He just likes the idea of being a barista, I think. He watched one documentary about coffee farmers in Colombia and suddenly he’s an expert on roast profiles. Which is fine, I guess, but it’s just so typical of him. Like that time he decided he was going to build a deck in the backyard and bought all that lumber, and it just sat under a tarp for two years until it rotted. I ended up having to hire a contractor to haul it away. The contractor was actually a really nice guy, though, his name was Mike, and he recommended this amazing Thai place near our house... 

Wait, what was the question? Acting on impulse? I mean, I guess I'm not really sure if I do that. I don't think I'm impulsive like my husband is.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or having trouble sitting still?

Fidgeting? Oh, absolutely. I definitely do that. Like, when I'm on calls with suppliers, my foot is usually just bouncing a mile a minute under the desk. And my hands, I'm always clicking a pen or twisting my ring around. It gets so bad I actually have to mute myself on the calls or move my hands completely out of view of the webcam so they don't see or hear me doing it. 

Speaking of webcams, they actually just upgraded all our tech at the office and gave everyone these little ring lights to clip onto our monitors. It makes me feel like I'm a beauty vlogger or something, which is just ridiculous because I'm literally just sitting there trying to negotiate wholesale pricing on bulk cashmere blends. Cashmere has gotten so outrageously expensive lately, by the way. We used to source this beautiful two-ply from a mill in Scotland, but they raised their minimum order quantities, so now we're looking at options in Inner Mongolia. The time difference for those calls is just brutal. I'm usually up at like 4 AM trying to talk to them, and I have to drink so much tea just to stay awake... 

Wait, why was I talking about the time difference? Oh! Sitting still. Right. Yes, I'm always twisting my ring or clicking my pens on those calls. I just can't seem to keep my hands and feet quiet.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?

Anxious or worried? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't feel like I'm sitting around worrying about things all the time. I'm usually just too busy to even think about it, honestly. 

Actually, speaking of being busy, my sister just decided she's going to host Thanksgiving this year, which is a complete shock because she hasn't cooked a turkey since 2008. She usually just orders one of those pre-cooked meals from the grocery store, which I always think tastes a little like cardboard, but I never say anything because it's easier, you know? But this year she bought this massive deep fryer. She watched one video on social media and now she thinks she's going to deep fry a twenty-pound bird in her driveway. I told her she’s going to burn her garage down. My neighbor actually did that a few years ago—well, not the garage, but he singed all the siding on his house. He had to get the whole side power-washed and repainted. It was this awful mustard yellow color before, but he changed it to a really nice slate gray, which looks so much better with his landscaping. He has these beautiful hydrangea bushes... 

But wait, what did you ask me? About being anxious? Yeah, no, I don't really feel anxious. I just have a lot going on.
Are your restless feelings and fidgeting causing problems for you at work or in your relationships?

Problems? Well, yeah, I guess it does cause some issues. At work, my planning coordinator has had to start double-checking things because I've rushed through and messed up some purchase orders. I just get so antsy sitting there looking at the spreadsheets. 

Speaking of spreadsheets, they just updated the software we use for inventory tracking, and it is a complete nightmare. They rolled it out on a Monday, which is already our busiest day, and nobody knew how to use it. The interface is completely different. It used to be this nice, clean grid, and now it's all these weird floating windows and pastel colors. Pastel colors for inventory management! It makes no sense. My coordinator, Sarah—she's usually so patient—even she was pulling her hair out. She ended up bringing in donuts on Wednesday just to keep everyone from quitting. They were from that little bakery down on 4th Street, the one with the pink awning? Their apple fritters are incredible. I used to go there all the time when I first moved to the city, back when I lived in this tiny studio apartment that didn't even have a real oven, just a hot plate...

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the problems it causes. Yeah, so work has been a little tense because of the purchase orders. And at home, too, honestly. Family dinners have gotten pretty stressful lately because everyone says I'm always talking over them or interrupting. I just get so restless sitting at the table!
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or following through on instructions?

Details? Oh, yeah, definitely. Over the past couple of years, it's gotten pretty noticeable. Like, I'll look over a vendor spreadsheet and I'll think I've checked it so carefully, you know? But then Sarah—my planning coordinator—she'll catch that I transposed a SKU, or I completely missed a freight surcharge, or I carried the wrong quantity into the purchase order. 

And freight surcharges are just out of control right now. I don't know if you've seen the news about the shipping containers, but it's a mess at the ports. We had a shipment of these gorgeous alpaca wool scarves stuck in Long Beach for three weeks. Three weeks! And then when they finally released them, the trucking company tried to tack on this ridiculous fuel surcharge. I spent like two hours on the phone arguing with this dispatcher named Gary. Gary sounded like he smoked three packs a day, just this really gravelly voice. He told me he used to drive a rig himself back in the eighties, hauling produce out of Florida. Or maybe it was Georgia? They have those really sweet peaches in Georgia. My grandmother used to make the most amazing peach cobbler every summer. She had this cast iron skillet that she swore was the secret, she never washed it with soap, just wiped it out with a paper towel... 

Wait, what was the question? Instructions and details? Right, yeah. The spreadsheets. I just miss things, like the SKUs and the quantities, even when I really try to focus.
Do you find it harder to pay attention to things or to sit still and keep from fidgeting?

Sit still? Oh, definitely the sitting still part. It's like I have this motor running inside me all the time. When I'm on calls with suppliers, my foot is usually just bouncing under the desk the whole time. And I don't even realize I'm doing it until my leg starts to get tired. I'm also constantly clicking a pen or twisting my ring around on my finger. It gets so bad I actually have to mute myself on the calls sometimes so they don't hear the clicking, or I have to consciously move my hands out of view of the camera. 

Actually, speaking of the camera, I just got this new webcam because my old one kept freezing right in the middle of sentences. It was so embarrassing. One time it froze while I was mid-sneeze, and my face was stuck like that for a solid two minutes while the supplier was talking about shipping delays. The new camera is one of those fancy 4K ones, and honestly, it's almost too good. Like, you can see every single pore on my face. I had to go out and buy this special ring light just to soften the shadows. The ring light has these three different color settings—warm, cool, and daylight. I usually use the daylight one, but my cat, Barnaby, he hates it. Whenever I turn it on, he just glares at me from the top of the bookshelf. He's this massive orange tabby, and he has so much attitude. He'll just sit up there and judge me. I adopted him from this little shelter downtown, the one right next to that amazing Italian place...

Wait, sorry, what was I talking about? Sitting still? Yeah, it's definitely the fidgeting. The bouncing foot, the pen clicking... it's just really hard for me to just sit there and not move.
Did you have trouble sitting still or paying attention when you were a kid?

Oh, as a kid? Yeah, definitely. I remember in elementary school, my mom was constantly getting notes sent home from my teachers because I kept popping out of my seat. My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to write them on this heavy pink stationery that smelled strongly of lavender. She was completely obsessed with lavender. She kept these little sachets of it all over the classroom, especially near the window where we kept the class guinea pig. His name was Marshmallow, and he was just this little white fluff ball. I was actually the one who usually got to feed him because, well, I was always up and out of my chair anyway, so I'd just wander over to his cage. 

I wanted a guinea pig of my own so badly after that, but my dad was allergic to dander, so we ended up getting a turtle instead. A red-eared slider named Speedy. We had him in this huge glass tank in the living room, and he lived for, gosh, maybe fifteen years? It's amazing how long turtles live. My cousin actually has a tortoise that's supposedly older than her. She keeps it in her backyard in Phoenix, and it just wanders around eating hibiscus flowers all day...

Wait, sorry, I'm doing it again. What did you ask? Oh, right, sitting still as a kid. Yeah, so besides popping out of my seat, the notes were also because I was always talking over my classmates. And I had this terrible habit of rushing to blurt out the answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. I just couldn't hold it in.
Did you act on impulse a lot when you were a kid?

Impulsive? Um, I don't really know if I was impulsive. I don't really remember doing things without thinking first, if that's what you mean. I mean, I guess I talked out of turn, like I said, but I don't remember doing dangerous things or, you know, acting on impulse. 

My brother, though, he was the impulsive one. Oh my gosh, the things he would do. One time, he decided he wanted to see if he could use a trash bag as a parachute, and he jumped off the roof of our garage. He broke his arm in two places. My mom was so mad, she wouldn't let him watch TV for a month. Which was a big deal back then, because we only had like three channels anyway, and Saturday morning cartoons were the highlight of the week. I loved the Smurfs. Did you know they made a live-action Smurfs movie a few years ago? It was terrible. The CGI was just... creepy. I took my niece to see it, and she actually started crying halfway through because Gargamel was too scary. We ended up leaving early and getting ice cream instead. She got mint chocolate chip, which is the best flavor, hands down. Although, I had this gelato in Italy once...

Sorry, what was the question? Impulsive? Right. No, I don't think I was really impulsive as a kid. Just the talking and the fidgeting.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?

Distracted? Um, no, not really. I feel like I can tune things out pretty well. I mean, my desk at home faces the front window, so there's always stuff going on outside, but it doesn't pull my focus away. Like, we have this massive oak tree right in the front yard, and there's a whole family of squirrels living in it. My neighbor, Susan, she actually bought one of those fancy squirrel-proof bird feeders last week because she was tired of them eating all her expensive sunflower seeds. But let me tell you, those things are absolutely not squirrel-proof. I watched one of them hang completely upside down from the gutter just to pry the lid off. They are so smart. 

Susan was furious when she saw. She takes her yard very, very seriously. I'm pretty sure she measures her grass with a ruler. She even bought this vintage manual push mower from an estate sale just to get the perfect cut. I actually love estate sales, though. I go to them almost every weekend. I guess being a buyer for my day job means I just naturally have an eye for a good deal. I found this absolutely stunning turquoise and silver brooch last month for like five dollars, and it turned out to be worth way more. I gave it to my sister for her fiftieth birthday. We went to this lovely little French bistro to celebrate, and the crème brûlée was just... 

Oh, gosh, wait, I lost my train of thought again. Distractions, right? Yeah, no, the stuff going on around me doesn't really bother me or pull me away from what I'm doing. I just keep working. Like I said, it's really just the physical bouncing and fidgeting that's the issue.
Have you experienced these restless feelings and fidgeting consistently since you were a kid?

Consistently? Um, well, I guess I've always been a bit squirmy, like I told you about elementary school. But it really hasn't been this bad the whole time. It's actually gotten noticeably harder to manage for, gosh, about two years and two months now? 

Yeah, it started getting really bad around the time these huge conflicts with my in-laws started taking over our evenings. My mother-in-law, she is just... well, she has a very specific way she thinks things should be done. Like Thanksgiving. She insists on hosting every single year, but she refuses to use the oven for the turkey. She bought this massive deep fryer, one of those outdoor ones, and my husband has to stand out in the freezing cold on the patio to watch it. Two years ago, he actually slipped on a patch of ice while he was carrying the peanut oil and spilled it everywhere. It was a complete disaster. The oil stained the concrete patio, and she made him go out there with a power washer the very next day, even though it was still below freezing. We had to order Chinese food for Thanksgiving dinner, which honestly, I preferred. I love a good lo mein. There's this place downtown that makes their own noodles from scratch, and you can actually watch them pulling the dough through the front window...

Wait, sorry. The fidgeting. Right. So, yeah, I've always been a little restless, but it really ramped up about two years and two months ago when the in-law drama started eating up all our free time.
Have you ever been diagnosed with ADHD or do you think you might have it?

ADHD? Um, no. No, I've never been diagnosed with that. I don't really think I have it, either. I mean, I'm just a bit restless, like I said. I don't really go to the doctor much for them to diagnose me with anything, honestly. 

My husband, though, he practically lives at the clinic. He just got diagnosed with sleep apnea a few months ago. They gave him one of those CPAP machines, and oh my word, it is so loud. It literally sounds like Darth Vader is sleeping next to me every night. I actually had to buy a white noise machine just to drown out the hissing. I found this really great one online that has like twenty different sound options. The thunderstorm one is my favorite, but there's this one that's supposed to be a crackling campfire, and it honestly just sounds like someone aggressively crinkling a bag of potato chips. Which is the worst sound when you're trying to sleep! Speaking of chips, did you know they changed the recipe for those kettle-cooked jalapeño ones? I used to order them by the pallet for the regional stores I buy for, but the new vendor uses way too much salt, and the sales just completely plummeted. I had to have this whole tense meeting with the distributor about the flavor profile, and he was so defensive... 

Wait, gosh, I'm doing it again. Sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, the ADHD thing. No, never been diagnosed with it. I'm really just here because the bouncing and squirming is driving me crazy.
Do you often interrupt others when they are speaking?

Interrupting? Um, well, I do catch myself doing that at work sometimes. Especially with the junior buyers. I'll hear them talking and I just cut right into their conversations to correct a detail or add my opinion before they’ve even asked for it. I really am just trying to support them, you know, rather than take over, because they're still learning the ropes. 

Like last week, we have this new girl, Chloe, and she was looking at a line of woven baskets from a new supplier. And I just had to jump in and interrupt because the shipping tariffs on those specific imports are just a complete nightmare right now. The logistics company we use—oh my gosh, they completely overhauled their tracking system in January, and it is a total disaster. It’s supposed to be this fancy cloud-based platform, but half the time it just logs you out in the middle of a shipping manifest. Our IT guy, Dave, he spent three hours on the phone with their customer support, and he said the guy on the other end had a rooster crowing in the background the entire time. A literal rooster! Can you imagine? Working from a farm sounds nice in theory, but I'm way too much of a city person. I love being able to just walk down to the corner and grab an espresso. There's this little café near my office that imports these incredible beans from Colombia, and the barista, Marco, he actually remembers my exact order every single time I walk in...

Oh, wait. Sorry. I completely lost track of what I was saying. You asked about interrupting. Yes, I definitely cut into the junior buyers' conversations to give my two cents. I really don't mean to be rude or take over, I just want to help them get it right.
Do you often forget things or have trouble remembering appointments and tasks?

Forget things? Um, no, not really. I mean, my memory is actually pretty sharp, especially for work stuff. I don't really miss appointments or anything like that. I keep a very detailed planner. 

Actually, speaking of planners, I just found this amazing new one at a stationery expo last month. It's bound in this gorgeous Italian leather, like a deep emerald green, and the paper is that really thick, creamy kind that doesn't bleed through when you use a fountain pen. I love fountain pens. My grandfather used to collect them, and he had this beautiful vintage Parker Vacumatic from the 1930s. He kept it in a velvet-lined cherry wood box on his desk, right next to this brass magnifying glass. He was a stamp collector, too. He had albums and albums filled with stamps from all over the world. I remember he had this one rare stamp from a tiny island nation that doesn't even exist anymore. I think it was somewhere in the Pacific? I always wanted to go to the Pacific, maybe Fiji or Bora Bora. I saw a documentary about those overwater bungalows, and they look absolutely incredible. You can literally just open a trapdoor in your living room floor and feed the fish...

Wait, sorry. What were we talking about? Oh, right, forgetting things. No, I don't really have a problem with that. My planner keeps me totally on track.
Have you experienced significant restlessness and fidgeting since you were a child?

Restlessness since I was a child? Oh, yeah, definitely. I mean, I remember back in elementary school, my teachers were always sending notes home to my parents because I just could not stay in my chair. I was always popping up, talking over the other kids, and blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question. 

My third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she was this really strict older woman who always wore these brightly colored, chunky beaded necklaces. She had this one necklace that looked like it was made out of giant gumballs, and I remember staring at it during spelling tests, wondering how heavy it was. Spelling was my favorite subject, though. We had this big spelling bee at the end of the year, and the prize was a gift certificate to the local bookstore. I love bookstores. Not the big chain ones, but those small, independent ones that smell like old paper and dust. There used to be this wonderful little shop downtown called The Book Nook, and the owner, Mr. Henderson, he had this fat orange tabby cat named Marmalade who would just sleep on top of the cash register all day. Marmalade was so lazy, you could literally stack paperbacks on him and he wouldn't even twitch. I tried to adopt a cat once, but it turns out my husband is terribly allergic. He broke out in hives within twenty minutes of me bringing the kitten home, so we had to take him back to the shelter. It was heartbreaking. The kitten, I mean, not the hives. My husband had to take Benadryl for three days...

Oh, gosh, I'm doing it again, aren't I? I'm so sorry. I just get going and I can't stop. What did you ask me? Right, the fidgeting as a kid. Yeah, I was definitely a squirmy kid, always jumping out of my seat and talking out of turn in class. It's just always been there, I guess.
Do you often have trouble following through on instructions or completing tasks?

Trouble finishing tasks? No, not really. I actually pride myself on seeing things through to the end, especially with my vendors. If I get an instruction from the merchandise director, or if I'm managing a purchase order, I make sure it's completed. 

Just last month we had this massive rollout for our spring patio line, and I had to coordinate with five different suppliers. One of them was doing these beautiful ceramic planters, hand-painted in Portugal. Have you ever been to Portugal? I went to Lisbon a few years ago with my sister, and the tile work on the buildings there is just breathtaking. Everywhere you look, there are these vibrant blue and white tiles—azulejos, they call them. We took this vintage yellow tram up a really steep hill, Tram 28 I think it was, and it was so crowded we had to stand the whole way, but the view of the water at the top was completely worth it. We stopped at this tiny bakery right near the viewpoint and had pastel de nata, those little custard tarts. Oh my goodness, they were warm right out of the oven, sprinkled with just a little bit of cinnamon. I actually tried to bake them at home once during the holidays, but my oven runs a little hot, so the puff pastry got way too dark. I really need to get the thermostat on that oven recalibrated. The appliance repair guy came out last year to look at the dishwasher, and I should have asked him to look at the oven then, but he didn't have the right part for the dishwasher anyway and it took three weeks to order...

Wait, sorry. I'm rambling again, aren't I? You were asking about following instructions and finishing things. Yeah, no, I don't really struggle with that at all. I'm pretty good at getting my work done and following through to the end.
Do you often have difficulty sustaining focus during tasks or activities?

Focusing? Um, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble focusing. I mean, I can really lock into my work when I need to. I review spreadsheets and inventory lists for hours. 

Actually, speaking of inventory, we just got a huge shipment of these artisanal woven baskets from Ghana. They're made of elephant grass, which I guess is incredibly durable. The colors are so vibrant—magenta, indigo, this really rich mustard yellow. They use natural dyes, which is so much better for the environment. I've been trying to be more eco-friendly at home, too. I started composting a few months ago, and I got this little stainless steel bin for the kitchen counter. It has a charcoal filter so it doesn't smell, but my husband still complains about it. He says it attracts fruit flies, but I think the fruit flies are actually coming from the bananas he insists on buying and then letting turn completely black. He makes banana bread with them, though, and it is really good. He adds walnuts and chocolate chips. I prefer pecans, but they're so expensive right now. I was at the grocery store on Tuesday, and a tiny bag of pecans was almost nine dollars! I ended up just buying almonds instead. Almonds are good for you anyway, lots of vitamin E. I read an article that said you should soak your almonds overnight before you eat them, something about breaking down the enzymes...

Oh, dear, I'm completely off track again. I'm sorry, my mind just goes a mile a minute. Focusing. Right. No, I don't really have a problem sustaining focus. If I have a task, I just buckle down and do it.
Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or following through on instructions?

Trouble with details? Well, I suppose... lately, yeah, maybe a little bit. Over the past couple of years, I'll be absolutely certain I've checked a vendor spreadsheet perfectly, line by line, and then our planning coordinator will come back and point out that I transposed a SKU, or I missed a freight surcharge, or carried the wrong quantity over to the final purchase order. 

It's so frustrating because I really do try to be careful. Speaking of freight, the shipping delays we've been dealing with have been an absolute nightmare. We had a container of holiday merchandise stuck at the port in Los Angeles for six weeks! Six weeks! By the time it got to our distribution center, half the stores had already set their seasonal displays. Have you ever tried getting a truck driver on the phone when a shipment is late? It's impossible. They use these satellite tracking systems now, which you'd think would make it easier, but half the time the signal drops out. My husband got a new GPS for his car because the built-in one kept trying to route him through cornfields when we drove out to visit his parents in Iowa. Iowa is so flat, but the sunsets there are actually really beautiful. We stopped at this roadside diner on the way, and they had the most incredible homemade cherry pie. The crust was so flaky, I asked the waitress what the secret was, and she said they use half butter and half lard. I know lard is terrible for your cholesterol, but my doctor—my primary care doctor, I mean—said my numbers were actually really good at my last physical. He told me to keep eating oatmeal. I buy the steel-cut kind, but it takes forever to cook on the stove, so I got one of those slow cookers...

Oh, goodness, I'm doing it again. The tangents! I am so sorry. You asked about details and instructions. But yes, like I was saying, I've definitely been making those silly little errors on my spreadsheets and purchase orders lately, even when I think I've checked them thoroughly.
Do you think your restlessness and fidgeting are more related to having trouble sitting still or to having trouble paying attention to things?

Restlessness? Oh, it's definitely the sitting still part. I mean, I just can't seem to stop moving. Like, when I'm on calls with suppliers—which is half my day, honestly—my foot is usually bouncing a mile a minute under the desk. And I'm always clicking a pen or twisting my wedding ring around and around. I actually have to mute myself sometimes because the pen clicking gets so loud, or I have to consciously move my hands out of view of the webcam so they don't see me fidgeting. 

Webcams are so unforgiving anyway, aren't they? I bought one of those ring lights to try and make the lighting better in my home office, but it just reflects off my glasses and makes me look like some kind of cyborg. I have these new frames, tortoise shell, from this boutique downtown. The girl who helped me pick them out had the most amazing bright pink hair. I've always wanted to dye my hair a fun color, maybe like a soft lavender, but I don't think it would look professional for vendor meetings. Plus, the upkeep! My friend Sarah went blonde last year and she's at the salon every four weeks for root touch-ups. She recommended this purple shampoo to keep it from getting brassy, and I accidentally used it when I stayed at her house... it stained my fingernails slightly purple for two days! I had a big presentation that week and I had to keep my hands in my lap the whole time...

Wait, hands. Fidgeting. Sorry, I'm doing it again. But yes, it's definitely a physical restlessness. I just have to be moving something, bouncing my foot, playing with a pen, twisting my ring... it's like I have all this extra energy that just has to get out somehow.

target_item.name: Feeling_Restless
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is this constant restless feeling, like I’m wound too tight and can’t fully settle, even when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting through a planning meeting, painting, or doing yoga.

patient.answer:
Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, what brings me in is just this... this constant restless feeling I've been having. It’s like I’m wound way too tight and I just can’t fully settle down, even when I’m supposed to be doing something really calm. 

Like, if I'm sitting through a planning meeting at work—I'm a retail buyer, so we have these endless strategy meetings. I was at the grocery store on Tuesday, and a tiny bag of pecans was almost nine dollars! I ended up just buying almonds instead. Almonds are good for you anyway, lots of vitamin E. I read an article that said you should soak your almonds overnight before you eat them, something about breaking down the enzymes...

Oh, dear, I'm completely off track again. I'm sorry, my mind just goes a mile a minute. Focusing. Right. No, I don't really have a problem sustaining focus. If I have a task, I just buckle down and do it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms meet the criteria for F90.8, F90.0, or F90.1 by asking about the presence of inattention
doctor.question: Do you often have trouble paying attention to details or following through on instructions?

target_item.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
target_item.manifestation: Over the past couple of years, I’ll think I’ve checked a vendor spreadsheet carefully, and then our planning coordinator catches that I transposed a SKU, missed a freight surcharge, or carried the wrong quantity into the purchase order.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about having trouble paying attention to details, which matches the symptom of failing to give close attention to details or making careless mistakes.

patient.answer:
Trouble with details? Well, I suppose... lately, yeah, maybe a little bit. Over the past couple of years, I'll be absolutely certain I've checked a vendor spreadsheet perfectly, line by line, and then our planning coordinator will come back and point out that I transposed a SKU, or I missed a freight surcharge, or carried the wrong quantity over to the final purchase order. 

It's so frustrating because I really do try to be careful. Speaking of freight, the shipping delays we've been dealing with have been an absolute nightmare. We had a container of holiday merchandise stuck at the port in Los Angeles for six weeks! Six weeks! By the time it got to our distribution center, half the stores had already set their seasonal displays. Have you ever tried getting a truck driver on the phone when a shipment is late? It's impossible. They use these satellite tracking systems now, which you'd think would make it easier, but half the time the signal drops out. My husband got a new GPS for his car because the built-in one kept trying to route him through cornfields when we drove out to visit his parents in Iowa. Iowa is so flat, but the sunsets there are actually really beautiful. We stopped at this roadside diner on the way, and they had the most incredible homemade cherry pie. The crust was so flaky, I asked the waitress what the secret was, and she said they use half butter and half lard. I know lard is terrible for your cholesterol, but my doctor—my primary care doctor, I mean—said my numbers were actually really good at my last physical. He told me to keep eating oatmeal. I buy the steel-cut kind, but it takes forever to cook on the stove, so I got one of those slow cookers...

Oh, goodness, I'm doing it again. The tangents! I am so sorry. You asked about details and instructions. But yes, like I was saying, I've definitely been making those silly little errors on my spreadsheets and purchase orders lately, even when I think I've checked them thoroughly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are primarily related to attention or hyperactivity
doctor.question: Do you think your restlessness and fidgeting are more related to having trouble sitting still or to having trouble paying attention to things?

target_item.name: Fidgeting
target_item.manifestation: On calls with suppliers, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk and I’m clicking a pen or twisting my ring so much that I have to mute myself or move my hands out of view.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the patient's fidgeting and trouble sitting still, which directly maps to the symptom of fidgeting, tapping hands/feet, or squirming in seat.

patient.answer:
Restlessness? Oh, it's definitely the sitting still part. I mean, I just can't seem to stop moving. Like, when I'm on calls with suppliers—which is half my day, honestly—my foot is usually bouncing a mile a minute under the desk. And I'm always clicking a pen or twisting my wedding ring around and around. I actually have to mute myself sometimes because the pen clicking gets so loud, or I have to consciously move my hands out of view of the webcam so they don't see me fidgeting. 

Webcams are so unforgiving anyway, aren't they? I bought one of those ring lights to try and make the lighting better in my home office, but it just reflects off my glasses and makes me look like some kind of cyborg. I have these new frames, tortoise shell, from this boutique downtown. The girl who helped me pick them out had the most amazing bright pink hair. I've always wanted to dye my hair a fun color, maybe like a soft lavender, but I don't think it would look professional for vendor meetings. Plus, the upkeep! My friend Sarah went blonde last year and she's at the salon every four weeks for root touch-ups. She recommended this purple shampoo to keep it from getting brassy, and I accidentally used it when I stayed at her house... it stained my fingernails slightly purple for two days! I had a big presentation that week and I had to keep my hands in my lap the whole time...

Wait, hands. Fidgeting. Sorry, I'm doing it again. But yes, it's definitely a physical restlessness. I just have to be moving something, bouncing my foot, playing with a pen, twisting my ring... it's like I have all this extra energy that just has to get out somehow.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of persistent restlessness, fidgeting, and difficulty sitting still, along with a history of similar behavior in childhood, align with the diagnostic criteria for Other Specified Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (F90.8). While the patient does exhibit some symptoms of inattention and impulsivity, they do not meet the full criteria for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Inattentive Type (F90.0) or Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive-Impulsive Type (F90.1).
